threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local, in-process Rust document engine that accepts DOCX/ZIP/XML, legacy DOC, Markdown, edit plans, images and fonts; compares, inspects, edits and resolves revisions; and produces DOCX, Markdown, PDF, PNG and reports. Supported execution paths are the native CLI, Rust API, Python native extension and facade, Python CLI, Python stdio MCP server, and Node/browser WASM bindings (README.md:13-17; src/lib.rs:96-165; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:45-59; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-35). Native CLI self-update and maintainer release publication are separate, privileged workflows. This model describes the live supplied checkout, observed HEAD 4e10eca69c42211651ca907f38b74b6d19e6928c, rather than inferring a revision from the scan output directory. Architecture mapping is not completed security-audit coverage.
assets: Confidential document contents, comments, authorship, embedded media and metadata; inspection text, rendered documents and reports disclose selected document data to their caller (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,194-218,245-255).

Integrity of source documents and exact edit targets. V1 plans can carry an optional source SHA-256; V2 plans require source.sha256 and refuse mismatches (src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-93).

Host files accessible to the native or Python process; MCP grants a persistent directory capability for document input and generated output, whereas ordinary CLI paths use ambient local authority (src/publication.rs:146-205; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278).

Process memory, CPU, raster memory and availability while parsing, comparing and rendering untrusted documents. Admission limits differ by operation and do not establish comprehensive process resource isolation (src/admission.rs:63-99; src/convert/mod.rs:602-630; SECURITY.md:71-74).

Native executable installation integrity: the updater installs a platform-specific GitHub release binary after checksum verification and an optional compiled-key signature policy (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Release publication authority and signing material: GitHub release write permission, optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, local Cargo/npm registry credentials, optional NPM_OTP and UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-263,278-307,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919-959,1063-1069).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted package bytes cross into the shared engine through admission and OPC parsing. Default agent inspection/editing limits are 64 MiB compressed, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison and rendering use 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total inflated, with the same entry/depth defaults. Explicit InputLimitOverrides replace individual base fields and reject unknown keys (src/admission.rs:63-108,137-163; src/inspect.rs:606-615; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778; src/document_comparer.rs:4927).

ZIP metadata crosses a parser-consistency boundary before normal package processing. Admission checks defects explicitly; the shared normal opener rejects divergent headers, overlapping extents and special entry types. Reads remain in memory rather than extracting document entries to the host filesystem. The debug diagnostic opener intentionally bypasses those structural refusals to inspect rejected packages (src/admission.rs:439-470,516-554; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Checked XML and permissive DOM parsing are distinct capabilities. Checked APIs apply well-formedness, tag and namespace policy; parse_xdocument deliberately does not enforce input policy, so direct library callers must validate first. Tag defaults include 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte attribute names, 64 MiB attribute values and 128 MiB start tags; other namespace limits also exist (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:44-65,84-114).

Edit requests cross from caller intent into document mutation. V1 hashes are optional, V2 source hashes mandatory; exact target resolution and shared preparation are separate from filesystem publication. Source hash agreement is a consistency guard, not caller authentication (src/edit.rs:2081-2094; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:74-93; src/edit/prepared.rs:185-230).

MCP clients invoke document tools through stdio, not an evidenced network listener. --root defaults to startup cwd; the expanded resolved root is opened once as a native OutputRoot. Input paths receive an early containment diagnostic, while actual reads and writes use the held cap-std directory capability. Explicit tool overwrite flags authorize replacing existing outputs; tool annotations are hints rather than an independent authorization mechanism (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199).

MCP output locations are root/out_dir/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json and optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png for editing; rendering uses root/out_dir/page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. OutputRoot validates portable relative paths, stages all files before committing, and commits atomically per file, not as one atomic set (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:161-218,229-255; src/publication.rs:100-143,168-199,228-245).

Native CLI filesystem publication is explicitly ambient: it opens and holds each selected parent directory and stages outputs. Python CLI and npm CLI have their own host filesystem adapters that read user paths and perform direct writes; those adapters must not inherit MCP confinement or native staged-publication guarantees by implication (src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-89,101-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-78,106-110).

Native rendering has an independent ambient font-reading capability. Document font names select installed-font searches; JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides platform user font directories. macOS/Unix defaults derive HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME; Windows uses APPDATA for Jubarte fonts and WINDIR/SystemRoot plus LOCALAPPDATA for installed fonts. macOS cloud fonts derive HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the direct family component is checked. Font bytes feed shaping and output generation (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2241-2255,2281-2315,2633-2652,2831-2862).

Browser WASM accepts byte inputs and returns byte/text results; host filesystem publication is excluded from wasm32, while the Node CLI itself supplies ambient Node filesystem operations. WASM uses the same Rust engine with default features disabled and cli enabled, and its release profile aborts on panic (src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-35,64-69; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-78,106-110).

Self-update crosses from GitHub release assets into replacement of the running executable. The repository is fixed to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, sums asset to SHA256SUMS.txt, and binary archive member to jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe]. It refuses noninteractive install without --yes or --check, checks the selected version, and verifies an extracted regular file. RELEASE_KEYS is currently empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so present builds consume checksum-only updates; Windows ZIP and Unix tar extraction are delegated to self_update (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,198-210,240-285,299-320).

Maintainer publication is separate from runtime document handling. Tag pushes v* trigger release builds with read-only contents permission; only the final release job has contents:write. Optional signing keys are decoded under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN with exit cleanup and passed to zipsign; release assets and SHA256SUMS.txt are uploaded using a job GITHUB_TOKEN supplied as GH_TOKEN. The local release script separately publishes to crates.io, npm and PyPI, with an explicit version confirmation unless --yes (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-25,51-55,230-307,317-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:875-899,919-959,1063-1069).

Native rendering also persists a font index outside the MCP document/output capability. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the location (empty/off disables it); otherwise the consumer reads/writes user_font_dir().parent()/font-index.tsv, with temporary extension tsv.<pid>.tmp. Defaults are $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv on macOS, $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv on Linux, and %APPDATA%\jubarte\font-index.tsv on Windows. With custom JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, the index is in that directory's parent. Recipients are the renderer, subsequent renderer processes and local readers permitted by host ACLs. Controls are trusted environment/configuration, delimiter filtering, cached length/mtime checks and write-then-rename; this is ambient std::fs authority, not OutputRoot confinement (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3090-3107,3154-3229,3264-3275).
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control package structure, XML, relationships, embedded media/fonts, document text, revision metadata, Markdown or legacy DOC bytes that a caller chooses to process. Such control does not grant host filesystem paths, trusted environment variables, operator credentials or release authority by itself.

A connected MCP client can request reads and supported document transformations within the server root and select output paths and overwrite flags there. The server intentionally grants that directory authority to its client; there is no evidenced per-tool principal separation or independent read-only client role (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-159,258-277,373-381).

An ordinary CLI user selects ambient input/output paths under their process permissions. Merely exercising those already-granted paths is not a privilege escalation; a meaningful failure would require document data or a lower-authority caller to gain additional unauthorized authority.

A hostile document can consume parser, comparison and rendering resources within effective input limits, including the materially larger comparison/render budgets. Shared-service impact requires a host deployment that accepts attacker inputs and shares finite process resources; no such network service or tenant deployment was supplied (src/admission.rs:63-99; SECURITY.md:71-74).

An attacker able to replace GitHub release archives and the adjacent checksum file could influence checksum-only update content; that requires release-asset control absent from a mere document supplier. Compiled release signature verification is not currently active (src/update.rs:44-48,245-285; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).
Control of trusted release tags, repository code or maintainer registry credentials is a separate supply-chain actor capability, not something inferred from untrusted document content.
securityObjectives: Reject malformed or ambiguous packages before normal processing, enforce effective compressed/inflated/XML budgets, and preserve safe in-memory package handling (src/admission.rs:439-554; src/opc/archive.rs:34-51).

Keep document relationships as document data rather than unintended host-file/network fetch authority. SECURITY.md states external relationships are not fetched; this architecture pass did not establish exhaustive caller coverage of every relationship consumer (SECURITY.md:71-74).

Bind guarded edits to exact source bytes, resolve all required targets before mutation is published, and keep optional V1 guards distinct from mandatory V2 guards (src/edit.rs:2081-2094; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-93).

Confine MCP document reads and generated outputs to the operator-granted root using actual capability-relative I/O, with explicit overwrite and reporting of partial commit/durability outcomes (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108; src/publication.rs:83-143,146-199).

Prevent data-controlled output names or symlink replacement from expanding filesystem authority, while preserving the intentionally broader ambient authority of ordinary CLI adapters (src/publication.rs:146-225,228-245).

Verify updater checksums and the applicable signature policy before replacing the executable; preserve the fixed repository/platform/member selection and regular-file check (src/update.rs:198-210,245-285,299-320).

Keep signing and registry credentials limited to their intended publication consumers and bind published artifacts to the selected version/source through release gates and artifact checks (.github/workflows/release.yml:40-49,261-307; scripts/release.sh:870-899,1063-1069).

Dependency implementations, generated WASM implementation parity, exhaustive parser coverage and actual remote account/registry configuration remain outside this focused architecture verification.

Font-index temporary writes use a predictable PID sibling and follow symlinks; exploitation needs another actor able to alter the configured cache parent. Default locations are under user data directories, and no shared writable cache deployment was provided. Document family names select lookup keys, not the configured cache destination (src/convert/font.rs:3090-3107,3213-3229).

findings.title: Converting a DOCX with a large table span can exhaust the host process
findings.summary: A small DOCX can place a very large positive value in `w:gridSpan`, `w:gridBefore` or `w:gridAfter`. PDF/PNG/report layout turns that value into vector lengths without a column budget, causing disproportionate allocation or an abort before returning a conversion error.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document producers can deterministically exhaust or abort the embedding renderer. Likelihood is high for a caller that converts attacker-supplied documents; impact is confined to availability of that process, with no established remote deployment.
severity.changeConditions: Dedicated subprocess limits reduce impact; an exposed shared conversion service would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects positive usize XML values to two unconditional allocation sites after admission; no semantic span cap exists on this path. No runtime reproduction was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource allocation from document metadata

codeEvidence.label: Public conversion enters admitted layout
codeEvidence.explanation: `docx_to_pdf`, PNG and reports share `with_layout`; admission limits ZIP/XML structure, then layout parses the body.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded cell span
codeEvidence.explanation: `w:gridSpan/@w:val` is parsed as `usize` with only a lower bound; the untrusted value becomes `RawCell.colspan`.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded omitted grid columns
codeEvidence.explanation: `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` likewise accept every positive `usize` and become synthetic cell spans.

codeEvidence.label: Span drives column allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Row occupancy becomes the length of a `Vec<f32>` without a semantic column limit.

codeEvidence.label: Span drives merge allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: The same span later sets the length of a vector of merge records, amplifying memory use.

rootCause.summary: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML.

findings.remediation: Apply a documented maximum table grid width to cell and omitted-column spans before raw-cell construction; use checked accumulation and reject over-budget occupancy before allocating or iterating. Enforce the same limit in merge bookkeeping.

counterEvidence: Package admission bounds compressed/inflated bytes, entry counts, XML attributes and depth.
SECURITY.md asks callers to apply CPU/memory process limits; those contain host impact but do not let the API return a bounded refusal.
limitations: No application code or vulnerability input was executed; no deployment exposure is asserted.
validation.summary: Validated public conversion -> admitted layout -> `cell_span`/`row_grid_skip` -> raw cell occupancy -> `Vec` expansion. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows whose used count exceeds existing columns and does not clamp hostile spans. Admission does not inspect grid span semantics.

dataflow.summary: DOCX XML span -> positive usize -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> column and merge vectors
dataflow.outcome: memory exhaustion, panic or process abort

impact.why: Availability of the CLI or embedding process; no confidentiality/integrity compromise established.

likelihood.why: A short decimal attribute directly controls allocation on an ordinary supported conversion path.

reachability.summary: The public in-process renderer accepts document bytes and uses this table parser after admission, which checks structure rather than numeric table semantics.
reachability.outcome: loss of availability of the rendering process
preconditions: Victim processes the supplied DOCX through layout; attacker needs no host filesystem/configuration access.

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid small DOCX containing a table cell with `w:gridSpan w:val="1000000000"`, then have the victim convert it to PDF/PNG or request page layout. The table model attempts multi-gigabyte allocation.

remediationTests: Convert a minimal admitted DOCX with a huge gridSpan and assert a typed resource refusal before allocating.
Cover huge gridBefore/gridAfter and multiple individually valid spans whose sum exceeds the grid budget.
preventiveControls: Use shared semantic allocation budgets for document-controlled counts in every layout path.

findings.title: Converting Markdown with cyclic drawing dependencies can abort the host
findings.summary: The `drawing:` image envelope accepts dependency indices but materializes them recursively without cycle detection or memoization. A tiny valid envelope in Markdown can make one dependency reference itself, causing unbounded recursion and allocations instead of a conversion error.

severity.rationale: A document producer can reliably terminate or exhaust the in-process converter through ordinary Markdown input. Impact is process availability; no remote service or privilege escalation is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A shared conversion service increases operational impact; a resource-limited disposable process contains it.

confidence.rationale: Parent source validation confirms an in-range self-reference takes the recursive branch repeatedly; the default public Markdown conversion path reaches materialization. No runtime trigger was executed.

taxonomy.category: Missing cycle control in document dependency graph

codeEvidence.label: Markdown accepts drawing envelopes
codeEvidence.explanation: A Markdown image destination beginning with drawing: is decoded and added as Content::Drawing without graph validation.

codeEvidence.label: Decoder only deserializes JSON
codeEvidence.explanation: Shallow attacker-controlled JSON becomes Drawing/Dep/PayRel objects, including integer dependency indices.

codeEvidence.label: Materializer follows the root index
codeEvidence.explanation: A root relationship part index selects dep_part if within deps length; cycles are not checked.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency traversal has no cycle detection
codeEvidence.explanation: Every dependent relationship recursively calls dep_part, with no active/visited index set, depth limit or memo table.

codeEvidence.label: Capture permits graph cycles
codeEvidence.explanation: DOCX capture memoizes a part before descending, so cycles can be encoded even by the trusted writer; capture limits do not protect materialization.

rootCause.summary: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

findings.remediation: Validate drawing dependency graphs on decode and materialization. Use a visited-index map with reserved output names before recursion, reject unsupported cycles, and enforce depth, dependency count and cumulative byte budgets independently of capture.

counterEvidence: DOCX capture limits parts, relationships and bytes and memoizes captured parts; the materializer neither reuses that memo nor validates graph cycles.
Caller process resource limits constrain availability impact but cannot turn stack overflow into a recoverable conversion error.
limitations: Static validation only; no malicious input or application code was executed.
validation.summary: Confirmed markdown_to_docx -> read/picture -> package::assemble/drawing -> materialize -> dep_part. Bounds checks prove indices exist but do not establish acyclicity. `used` is a name-collision set rather than a graph-visit set. serde recursion limits concern nested JSON, not integer graph cycles.

dataflow.summary: Markdown drawing: URI -> base64/serde graph -> Content::Drawing -> package materialize -> repeated dep_part(0)
dataflow.sink: recursive dependency traversal with per-call allocation
dataflow.outcome: stack overflow/process abort or memory exhaustion

impact.why: Terminates or exhausts the current process.

likelihood.why: A small shallow JSON envelope can express the required integer cycle.

reachability.summary: Public markdown::markdown_to_docx accepts the Markdown directly; CLI and bindings wrap this library boundary. No image-loader callback or filesystem authority is needed.
preconditions: A victim converts the supplied Markdown.

attackPath.summary: Have the victim convert Markdown containing a `drawing:` JSON envelope with a root dependency 0 and a dependency relationship back to 0. Default conversion reaches recursive materialization and cannot return normally.

remediationTests: Convert an inline drawing envelope with a self-cycle and assert a bounded typed refusal.
Cover a two-node cycle, deep acyclic chain, repeated shared dependency and over-budget graph.
preventiveControls: Treat integer-indexed serialized graphs as untrusted graphs rather than assuming capture-produced invariants.

findings.title: Reading a small legacy DOC can expand reused text into billions of records
findings.summary: Legacy DOC pieces can map many contiguous logical text ranges to the same physical bytes. The reader decodes one `StoryChar` per logical character without an output/work budget, so a roughly megabyte input can exhaust the host long before a resulting DOCX is admitted.

severity.rationale: Input-controlled logical expansion can cause very large memory/CPU consumption in a victim process. Likelihood is high when legacy documents are accepted; impact is bounded to availability with no supplied shared deployment.
severity.changeConditions: Resource-limited per-document subprocesses reduce collateral impact; a shared public conversion worker would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static arithmetic and dataflow establish repeated physical ranges yielding independently appended logical characters. Structural checks do not bound cumulative logical output; no runtime resource-exhaustion probe was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Legacy parser decodes before other story tables
codeEvidence.explanation: The public read API loads the piece table and immediately expands its logical story.

codeEvidence.label: Attacker selects logical character count
codeEvidence.explanation: The FIB ccp_text field is read from the untrusted WordDocument stream as a u32.

codeEvidence.label: Each piece selects its own physical text offset
codeEvidence.explanation: Logical CPs and physical fc are independent; compressed pieces may reuse the same source range.

codeEvidence.label: Logical characters drive record construction
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP consumes decoding work and appends a StoryChar without a cumulative output budget.

codeEvidence.label: CLI converts DOC before DOCX admission
codeEvidence.explanation: The legacy branch calls doc_to_docx first and is excluded from the ordinary DOCX admission step.

codeEvidence.label: CLI refusal hint parses legacy input too
codeEvidence.explanation: The shared read_document helper invokes legacy_doc::read even to decide whether to suggest conversion after a format refusal, so a refused legacy input can reach the same expansion before a hint is returned.

rootCause.summary: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.

findings.remediation: Enforce maximum logical decoded character/output-work budget before allocating StoryChar; thread configurable legacy limits into public and CLI conversion.

counterEvidence: Physical sector/DIFAT chains bounded by input and duplicate FAT sectors rejected.
Physical character reads bounds checked; logical CP coverage must be increasing/contiguous.
Policy recommends caller process limits; no decoder output-work budget.
Static only; no exploit execution.
limitations: No application execution or generated malicious document was used.
validation.summary: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.

findings.title: Checking a DOCX dialect can inflate an unbounded root tag
findings.summary: The public `main_part_is_strict` detector reads compressed XML without admission or an actual-inflation cap. A long root opening tag retains an ever-growing buffer that is rescanned after every 16 KiB read, allowing a small compressed input to exhaust memory or CPU.

severity.rationale: An attacker-controlled document can exhaust a process using this public parser API. The deterministic input-to-resource path makes likelihood high at this boundary; impact is availability, and no production caller or remote deployment is inferred.
severity.changeConditions: Independent input admission reduces memory amplification; a streaming bounded scanner removes the failure. Shared worker use would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct static trace shows no limits around decompression or accumulation, and retaining '<' at offset zero prevents buffer release. No runtime probe or in-repository production caller established.

codeEvidence.label: Public boolean detector opens compressed part
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller bytes open directly through the structural archive checker; the function does not admit or apply InputLimits.

codeEvidence.label: Growing root tag has no inflation/work cap
codeEvidence.explanation: The part is read repeatedly, retained from its last '<', and rescanned each iteration without a counting cap.

codeEvidence.label: Detector is externally reachable
codeEvidence.explanation: The module is public, so callers can use this detector independently of the normal admitted conversion entrypoints.

rootCause.summary: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '<' and no '>', draining before the last '<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

findings.remediation: Enforce actual-inflation and start-tag bounds and parse incrementally.

counterEvidence: open_archive verifies ZIP header consistency/extent/type, not inflation bounds.
strict_to_transitional_docx_within bounds inflation but sibling main_part_is_strict does not.
No in-repo production callers found; boundary is public API.
Caller may admit first; still expensive repeated scans within admitted bytes.
limitations: No application or exploit input was executed; caller deployments and external resource isolation are unknown.
validation.summary: Verified the public export and standalone detector; the only opener enforces structural ZIP consistency, not InputLimits. The sibling normalization API uses inflation budgets, but this detector bypasses them. No in-repository production call reaches the detector; the claim is limited to direct public library use.

findings.title: Publishing a release exposes the PyPI token in process arguments
findings.summary: The release script takes the operator's reusable `UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN` from the environment and passes its value as `uv publish --token`. Another local user who can inspect command lines during publication can obtain the publishing credential.

severity.rationale: Potential registry publication authority is sensitive, but exploitation requires a separate local account with process-command-line visibility during a brief privileged release operation. Token scope and multi-user deployment are unknown; these prerequisites make likelihood low.
severity.changeConditions: A shared release host with readable process command lines increases likelihood; restricted process visibility or removing the argument eliminates this route.

confidence.rationale: Source proves secret-to-argv flow. Host process visibility, uv argument scrubbing timing, actual token scope and live validity were not tested.

findings.title: Inspecting a DOCX relationship can trigger quadratic CPU work
findings.summary: OPC relationship targets are decoded by the dependency and then unescaped again by `PartFs::resolve_rel_target`. A well-formed Target made of repeated `&` becomes literal ampersands, each causing a scan of the entire remaining string. Inspection and comparison can spend quadratic CPU time before rejecting a missing part.

severity.rationale: An ordinary untrusted package can monopolize the embedding process within default byte/XML limits. Likelihood is high for inspection/comparison of supplied packages; impact is process availability without an inferred shared service.
severity.changeConditions: A linear decoder/removing redundant decoding closes the path; dedicated CPU-limited subprocesses contain worker impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent inspected local oxml-opc target normalization and source-to-sink callers; the suffix loop demonstrably performs N(N-1)/2 comparisons for N ampersands. Static only.

rootCause.summary: `read_relationships` loads each record through oxml-opc, whose `parse_relationship` applies `decoded_and_normalized_value` before storing Target. Internal consumers pass that decoded string to `PartFs::resolve_rel_target`, which invokes `unescape_xml_text` again. For N escaped ampersands in source, the second pass sees N literal ampersands and no semicolons. Each failed semicolon search revisits the suffix, then advances by one, yielding N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Attribute count, XML depth and package byte limits do not bound this quadratic work adequately.

findings.remediation: Treat upstream Relationship.target as decoded data and remove redundant XML decoding. Make unescape_xml_text linear even for malformed references, and enforce practical relationship-target/work bounds.

findings.title: Admitted DOCX XML can bypass the DOM nesting limit
findings.summary: Admission and the permissive DOM disagree about unquoted attribute syntax. A crafted root tag hides thousands of apparent child tags inside an attribute for admission, then exposes them as nested elements to the DOM, bypassing the 256-level limit and exhausting the stack.

severity.rationale: Small supplied document data can terminate the process through deep DOM recursion despite admission. Likelihood is high for the evidenced WmlDocument path; impact is process availability. Strict inspect XML paths reject the malformed attribute and are not claimed vulnerable.
severity.changeConditions: Using strict checked XML consistently or enforcing depth in DOM construction removes the path; isolated worker limits reduce collateral impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced both parsers and the WmlDocument caller and read local quick-xml quote/normalization logic. Static construction demonstrates different nesting interpretations without executing it.

codeEvidence.explanation: For a=x the delimiter becomes x; consuming through the next x can move an attribute's hidden '>' into the element boundary.

codeEvidence.label: DOM recursion has no independent depth guard
codeEvidence.explanation: Each newly exposed '<n>' recursively calls parse_element, even though admission saw those bytes inside a quoted attribute.

rootCause.summary: Admission uses quick-xml's event scanner and HTML attribute iterator, which treats `a=x b="x>..."` as one unquoted and one quoted attribute. Literal `<n>` strings within b remain attribute content, so admission sees a shallow document. The DOM parser instead treats the first x after a= as a quote delimiter and consumes through b's first x. It then treats the next `>` as the root-tag end, exposing the hidden `<n>` strings as elements. Recursive child parsing has no independent depth limit, so a roughly 300 KiB attribute containing 100,000 `<n>` strings can cause 100,000 recursive calls despite an admitted depth of one.

findings.remediation: Use the same attribute grammar for admission and DOM construction and enforce depth while building the DOM. Reject unquoted attributes on untrusted paths, or correctly parse them as unquoted values rather than arbitrary delimiters.
